messages:
sam: quick check — noticed 99th pctl tail spikes on small-batch (n=1..4) inference when we pin non-contiguous host pages for offload. spikes show up only under mixed tenant load. anyone else seen this?

maya: yep, saw something similar last week while triaging a regression. looks like page-list walking + TLB churn when we build the scatter/gather for the staged buffers.

derek: can you paste a short stack/log? curious if it's the `get_user_pages` path or our staging allocator doing a lot of small `mmap`/munmap` ops.

sam: here's the minimal repro logs we captured:
```
evictor: pin_range 0x7f8a..0x7f9b len=64k tenant=42
staging: sg entries=8 stride=4k build_time=2.1ms
kernel: tlb_miss_count += 120
latency: request=42ms median=8ms p99=210ms
```

chloe: that `sg entries=8` is the clue. when we create many tiny SG entries for a single token stream we pay a huge amortized cost building the descriptors and walking the memmap. fragmentation increases SG count.

maya: tradeoffs: either (A) coalesce host pages into contiguous pinned extents before SG build (need compaction/copy), (B) keep SG but batch through a fastpath that prefetches/locks user mappings in one syscall, or (C) accept higher p99 and rely on tenant isolation + backpressure.

derek: (A) reduces runtime overhead but adds CPU & extra copy cost and complicates the allocator API (move + update KVCaches). (B) seems promising if we can do a single syscall to grab a larger window of PTEs; may require kernel changes or risk with `MLock` semantics.

chloe: also consider quantile-targeted policies: if request predicted latency budget < 50ms, prefer contiguous coalescing; otherwise SG fastpath. that gives QoS control per route.

sam: good point. what's the implementation surface for coalescing? I was thinking a cooperative compact call on the host staging pool: try up to N bytes of consolidation, copy, then update staging handles atomically.

maya: sketch:
```
// host-staging API
int consolidate_range(staging_pool_t *p, addr_t begin, size_t want_len, addr_t *new_base);
// returns contiguous guest-host mapping with pins held
```

maya: fallback if consolidation fails: record fragmentation metric and route to slower class. we should expose telemetry: SG_count, consolidate_attempts, consolidate_success, extra_copies.

derek: we'll need to audit our eviction & lease code — moving pages while a KV reference exists needs a short quiesce window or indirection. maybe introduce a versioned pointer in the KVCace entry so reads can switch atomically.

chloe: performance estimate: coalesce 256KB copy cost ~0.12ms on our nodes (memcpy + pin ops), but avoids dozens of per-entry syscall overheads which were ~1-2ms cumulatively. so net win for tight p99 targets.

sam: sounds promising. risks: increased CPU, potential regressions for huge tenants, and complexity around cross-tenant compaction fairness.

maya: proposed next steps: 1) implement consolidation API prototype in host staging (opt-in flag) 2) add SG fastpath that does a bulk lock syscall when SG_count > threshold 3) add telemetry + route QoS knob 4) RFC follow-up to cover lease/versioning semantics.

chloe: +1. can we also run an experiment with tenant-weighted compaction so big tenants don't starve others? simple budget token per-tenant should work.

derek: will put up a small design PR for the consolidation API today and a perf microbenchmark that toggles it. tagging infra-bot to kick off a perf run: @infra-bot please run with mixed-tenant synthetic load (small-batch N=1..4) across 3 instances and collect p50/p95/p99, SG_count, consolidate_attempts.

infra-bot: perf job queued: job_id=perf-9177770001-01, expected runtime ~45m. artifacts -> /perf/artifacts/perf-9177770001-01

sam: thanks — after perf we can decide if this becomes default for latency-sensitive routes. i'll open the RFC stub for the lease indirection changes. :thumbsup:
